en: The Sūtra on the Dhāraṇī of the Adornment of the Tathāgata Invincible Banner King,
spoken by the Buddha at the Indrasālā Monastery in the kingdom of Uḍḍiyāna, North India.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master, the Purple-Robed Śramaṇa and Subject Shi Hu, by Imperial Decree. Thus have I heard.
At one time, the World-Honored One was dwelling in the Sudharmā Hall within the palace of Śakra, Lord of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, amidst a great assembly.
At that time, there suddenly appeared an asura king,
accompanied by his retinue and military hosts;
each was clad in armor and held weapons in their hands.
Surrounding him from all sides, they came to engage in battle and launched an assault upon the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven.
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, together with the hosts of devas...
Adorned with precious armor and wielding weapons, he engaged them in battle.
At that time, the host of the Asura King achieved victory;
the assembly of the Trāyastriṃśa devas was defeated and, struck with fear, fled in all directions.
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas,
concealed his celestial majesty and manifested the appearance of an ordinary person,
then hurriedly galloped forth to visit the World-Honored One.
Having arrived at the Buddha’s dwelling, he prostrated at the Buddha’s feet and addressed him, saying,
"World-Honored One, I have now come with the various hosts of the Asura King to wage war against you."
The assembly of the Trāyastriṃśa gods dispersed in fear and fled in all directions,
thinking, "By what means can we be rescued from this calamity?
At that time...
The Buddha addressed Śakra, Lord of the Devas, saying:
"Listen attentively, and I shall explain it for you.
There is a dhāraṇī named 'Adorned with the Invincible Banner.'"
In the past, when I was a bodhisattva,
there was a Buddha named Anabhibhūtavaijayantadhvajarāja Tathāgata; from that Buddha, I heard this dhāraṇī.
From that time forth, I have also extensively expounded this Dharma for others and have obtained great auspicious signs;
yet, not even for the duration of a finger-snap has there ever been any cause for fear.
At that time, the Buddha again addressed Śakra, Lord of the Devas, saying:
"I shall now recite for you this *Ajita-dhvaja-vyūha-dhāraṇī*: Tadyathā | jaye | vijaye |"
Jaya vijaya sañjaya vāhini saṃkare pracaṇḍe sarvaduṣṭān vaśamānaya vaśamānaya svāhā.

112. *naukṣatra* 113. *dharmigrahaṇa* 114. *svāhā*. The Buddha addressed Śakra, Lord of the Devas, saying:
This Aparājitadhvajavyūha-dhāraṇī shall constantly provide protection for me both internally and externally;
you should uphold this dhāraṇī.
Make a pouch using multicolored silks, place [the object] therein, and tie it to the top of your banner. Wherever you go,
whether you are fighting, quarreling, or killing with other enemies, [it shall protect you].
Whether you engage in verbal disputes with others or in any other situation, there shall be no place where you do not achieve victory.
You should transcribe this dhāraṇī, place it in a pouch, and tie it around your neck; it will protect and sustain you.
I, too, shall act as a protector in all places for the sake of future generations and for the benevolent kings of the world.
That is the Tathāgata Aparājita-dhvaja-rāja.
Manifesting in the form of a goddess before one's face,
she bestows fearlessness, provides protection, and secures victory;
she causes the enemy forces to be scattered and defeated.
If a benevolent king is further able to copy, disseminate, uphold,
read, and recite this dhāraṇī,
he shall constantly obtain pure and auspicious matters.
No external enemies or adversaries shall be able to prevail over them.
When the Buddha had finished preaching this sutra,
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, and the assembly of devas [rejoiced].
Having heard what the Buddha had spoken, they were all greatly rejoiced;
they accepted it with faith, practiced accordingly, prostrated, and withdrew.
This concludes the *Buddha-spoken Sūtra of the Dharani of the Adornment of the Invincible Banner*.
